messages.author: e29864cff159cb09
messages.subject: Caching of Objects
parts:
It seems like once Shiny Server has loaded an object (like a CSV or an R workspace) that object is cached for future sessions. But sometimes you want to have that app load a new object (even if it has the same name) and yet the cached version keeps loading.

A couple of questions:

1. Am I crazy or is what I describe above built in behavior?
2. Is there any way to clear out cached objects so that the next time the app runs it will re-load the object (like if you changed some of the underlying data in an object)?

Thx.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Caching of Objects
parts:
Whether an object is "cached" across all sessions or not is determined by which scope you use when loading it:
http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping

You can get the best of both worlds by using the new reactiveFileReader function, and calling it above the server function. This way, it'll be visible across all sessions, but it'll automatically update itself when the file changes on disk, and trigger reactive expressions and observers/outputs that depend on it.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Caching of Objects
parts: You would use rm(), the same as removing any other objects from any other environment in R. However, like any other R script, if there are references to these objects being maintained in the sessions, those don't automatically disappear (it would be really confusing if they did--like dangling pointers in C).
